docs.title: mallops
docs.text:
Modular MLOps in Rust — from data ingestion to edge devices, one block at a time.

Early stage

mallops is in the design phase. The specification and architecture are open for feedback.

docs.title: Why mallops
docs.text:
• Every MLOps step is a block — ingestion, storage, preprocessing, training, model engineering, evaluation, packaging, versioning, deploy, serving, monitoring, retrain. Add, remove or replace any of them.
  • Bring any model, any library — ONNX, safetensors, TorchScript, pickle, GGUF, XGBoost, your own format.
  • Three ways to use it — Rust library, plugins (WASM or external processes in any language), or standalone with YAML and the mallops CLI.
  • Edge-ready — local serving, distributed monitoring and federated learning on devices.
  • Reproducible — content-addressed artifacts, lineage for every run, cached re-runs.
flowchart LR
    I[Ingest] --> S[(Data storage)] --> P[Preprocess] --> T[Train] --> E[Evaluate]
    E -->|gate| K[Package] --> V[Version] --> D[Deploy] --> SV[Serve]
    SV --> M[Monitor] -->|drift| R[Retrain] --> T
    D --> EDGE[Edge devices] -. federated updates .-> T

docs.title: mallops — Architecture
docs.text: Companion to SPEC.md. Decisions are recorded in adr/.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph User
        Y[mallops.yaml]
        L[Rust code]
    end
    subgraph Core["mallops-core"]
        P[Config parser + validator]
        G[DAG builder]
        R[Runtime / scheduler]
        REG[Block registry]
        S[(ArtifactStore trait<br/>local · memory)]
        LIN[Lineage events<br/>JSON sink]
    end
    subgraph Backends["Optional backends"]
        RS3[(S3 / GCS / Azure)]
        LS[SQLite · OpenLineage · MLflow]
    end
    S -.-> RS3
    LIN -.-> LS
    subgraph Blocks
        STD[mallops-std<br/>feature-gated]
        RS[User Rust blocks]
        W[WASM components]
        X[External process<br/>gRPC / CLI]
    end
    Y --> P --> G --> R
    L --> G
    REG --> R
    R <--> S
    R --> LIN --> S
    STD & RS --> REG
    W & X --> REG

The core knows only three things: blocks, artifacts, and the graph between them. Everything ML-specific lives in blocks.

Store and lineage are not blocks: blocks are nodes of the DAG, while store and lineage act on every edge. The core owns their contracts and a minimal default; every real backend is optional (ADR-0006).

docs.title: 2. Workspace layout
docs.text:
mallops/
├── crates/
│   ├── mallops-core/   # traits, artifacts, store & lineage contracts, config, runtime
│   ├── mallops-cli/    # `mallops` binary              (v0.1)
│   ├── mallops-std/    # standard blocks, feature-gated (v0.1)
│   └── mallops-edge/   # edge agent + FL aggregator     (v0.4)
├── docs/
└── examples/

Crates are created only when implemented. Splitting mallops-std into per-stage crates is deferred until compile times or dependency weight demand it (ADR-0001).

Crate Depends on Dependencies mallops-core — Core allowlist: tokio, serde, serde_json, blake3, tracing, thiserror, ulid, tempfile; optional features: yaml (yaml_serde, default), schema (schemars) (ADR-0007) mallops-std core workspace blake3, serde, serde_json, tokio (already in the graph via core); optional behind per-block Cargo features (--no-default-features pulls in no Arrow or Parquet crate): ingest-csv (arrow-csv 59), ingest-parquet, meta-feature ingest = ["ingest-csv", "ingest-parquet"] (default), sharing internal _ingest (arrow-array 59, arrow-schema 59, parquet 59 with default-features = false, features = ["arrow", "snap", "lz4", "flate2-zlib-rs", "zstd"] — pinned to 59 because 60 requires Rust 1.88 > MSRV 1.85; codecs are for reading external Parquet files while outputs stay uncompressed); future features: linfa, ort, axum, object_store (store-s3, store-gcs, store-azure), rusqlite (lineage-sqlite), … mallops-cli core, std clap (derive), anyhow, serde_json, tracing-subscriber (fmt), tokio (rt-multi-thread); dev: insta, tempfile mallops-edge core, std (profile-edge, ADR-0008) tonic, rumqttc (via serve-mqtt)

mallops-std exposes pub fn register_std(registry: &mut BlockRegistry) -> Result<(), Error>, registering only the blocks whose Cargo features are enabled and returning Error::Validation if a block id is already registered. std/ingest.csv and std/ingest.parquet share the internal ingest module: expected schema columns (bool | int64 | float64 | string | date32), uncompressed data.parquet output with fixed created_by: "mallops-std" (kind: dataset, format: parquet; deterministic per mallops-std version, source schema/field metadata stripped), streamed BLAKE3 extra_hash in CachePolicy::Deterministic, and tokio::task::spawn_blocking with between-batch CancelToken checks for file I/O and conversion (relative paths resolve against the process cwd, which mallops run sets to the directory of mallops.yaml). Known v0.1 limitations are documented in SPEC §3.1 (TOCTOU between cache_policy and run, and inferred CSV types Null/Timestamp outside the schema: subset).

docs.title: 3. Core abstractions
docs.text:
Extensible public structs and enums are marked #[non_exhaustive] with dedicated constructors/builders so new fields and variants remain semver-compatible toward 1.0 (ADR-0007).

/// Static description of a block: identity, version, I/O ports, optional config schema.
#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct BlockSpec {
    pub id: Cow<'static, str>,               // "std/train.external"
    pub version: Cow<'static, str>,          // "0.1.0" (included in cache key & lineage)
    pub stage: Stage,                        // Ingest, Preprocess, Train, …
    pub inputs: Vec<Port>,                   // name + kind + accepted formats/flavors (empty = any) + required
    pub outputs: Vec<Port>,
    pub config_schema: Option<serde_json::Value>, // decoupled from `schemars`
}

#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum BlockOutcome {
    Produced(OutputDrafts),                  // runtime commits drafts to ArtifactStore
    Skipped { reason: String, outputs: OutputDrafts },
}

#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum CachePolicy {
    Deterministic { extra_hash: Option<Digest> },
    Uncacheable,
}

pub trait Block: Send + Sync {
    fn spec(&self) -> &BlockSpec;
    fn validate_config(&self, config: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<(), Error> { Ok(()) }
    fn resolve_ports(&self, config: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<ResolvedPorts, Error> { /* default: spec ports */ }
    // `'a` on self and ctx: the future may use `ctx` (cancel, secrets, config, workdir).
    fn cache_policy<'a>(&'a self, ctx: &'a Context) -> BoxFuture<'a, Result<CachePolicy, Error>>;
    fn run<'a>(&'a self, ctx: &'a Context, inputs: Inputs) -> BoxFuture<'a, Result<BlockOutcome, Error>>;
}

/// `name` + `kind` + accepted `formats`/`flavors` (empty = any; several = any of them).
/// `required` defaults to `true`; `Port::optional()` clears it (read with `Inputs::try_get`).
#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct Port { pub name: Cow<'static, str>, pub kind: ArtifactKind,
    pub formats: Vec<Cow<'static, str>>, pub flavors: Vec<Cow<'static, str>>, pub required: bool }

/// Owned payload of an `OutputDraft` (`PayloadSource` borrows, so it cannot live in a draft).
/// The runtime must confine `File`/`Dir` paths inside `ctx.workdir()` before `put`.
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum DraftPayload { File(PathBuf), Dir(PathBuf), Bytes(Vec<u8>), Files(BTreeMap<RelPath, Vec<u8>>) }

/// Given to each block during execution (runtime instruments `run()` with a tracing span).
/// Fields are private; blocks read them through accessors.
#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct Context { /* run_id, workdir, store, config, cancel, secrets */ }
impl Context {
    pub fn run_id(&self) -> RunId;
    pub fn workdir(&self) -> &Path;                          // scratch dir, also mounted for external blocks
    pub fn store(&self) -> &Arc<dyn ArtifactStore>;
    pub fn config(&self) -> &serde_json::Value;              // `with:` with `${env:…}` resolved; NEVER contains secrets
    pub fn cancel(&self) -> &CancelToken;                    // cooperative cancellation (`watch::Receiver<bool>`)
    pub fn secret(&self, name: &str) -> Result<Secret, Error>;
    pub fn config_as<T: DeserializeOwned>(&self) -> Result<T, Error>;
}
// Blocks never touch lineage and never call `store.put()` for outputs:
// the runtime commits outputs, injects `parents`, validates ports, and emits lineage events.

#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct Artifact {
    pub id: ArtifactId,                      // validated 32-byte canonical BLAKE3 digest
    pub manifest: Manifest,                  // schema_version, kind, format, flavor, io_schema, metadata, parents
}

#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum ArtifactKind { Dataset, Features, Transform, Model, Metrics, Package, Blob }

#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum Error {
    Config(String),
    Validation(Vec<ValidationError>),        // all problems of one pass; ValidationError { path, message }
    Store(StoreError),
    Runtime(String),
    Cancelled,
    Secret(String),
    InvalidArtifactId(String),
    InvalidPath(String),
    Block { id: String, source: Box<dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync> },
}

/// Runtime settings: `new(store)` defaults to available parallelism, `EnvSecretProvider`,
/// `std::env::temp_dir()`, a cancel token that never fires, one `JsonSink` on `store`,
/// `SystemTime::now`, `HostInfo::current()`, and `git_commit: None`.
#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct RuntimeConfig {
    pub max_jobs: usize,                     // `--jobs`; 0 counts as 1
    pub store: Arc<dyn ArtifactStore>,
    pub secret_provider: Arc<dyn SecretProvider>,
    pub workdir_root: PathBuf,               // per-run temporary workdirs are created here
    pub cancel: CancelToken,                 // external cancellation, seen by blocks via ctx.cancel()
    pub no_cache: bool,                      // `--no-cache`: every node runs, no cache entry read or written
    pub lineage: Vec<Arc<dyn LineageSink>>,  // empty = `lineage: off`; YAML mapping lives in `mallops-cli`
    pub clock: fn() -> SystemTime,           // injectable for deterministic tests
    pub host: HostInfo,                      // recorded in `RunStarted`
    pub git_commit: Option<String>,          // `None` in core; set by `mallops run` via `git rev-parse HEAD`
}

pub struct Runtime { /* config */ }
impl Runtime {
    pub fn new(config: RuntimeConfig) -> Self;
    // Err only for runtime failures; node outcomes are in the summary.
    pub async fn run(&self, pipeline: &ValidatedPipeline) -> Result<RunSummary, Error>;
}

#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct RunSummary { pub run_id: RunId, pub nodes: BTreeMap<String, NodeSummary> } // is_success()

#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct NodeSummary {
    pub status: Status,
    pub duration: Duration,                  // zero if the node never started or its task panicked
    pub outputs: BTreeMap<String, ArtifactId>, // committed outputs by port
    pub reason: Option<String>,              // why skipped / cancelled
    pub error: Option<Error>,                // Failed node, or Error::Cancelled from a cancelled block
    pub cached: bool,                        // outputs served from the cache, block not run
}

#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum Status { Succeeded, Failed, Skipped, Cancelled }
  • Validation: PipelineConfig::validate(&BlockRegistry) -> Result<ValidatedPipeline, Error> checks DAG, resolved ports, with: configs and serve.package in one pass without running any block, aggregating ValidationError { path, message } (dotted paths such as blocks.eval.in.test, see SPEC §5). ValidatedPipeline holds nodes in topological order (ties by id), each with its Arc<dyn Block>, BlockConfig and ResolvedPorts. PipelineBuilder builds the same PipelineConfig in Rust, available without the yaml feature, and build(&registry) goes through the same validator.
  • Secrets (Secret): opaque newtype whose Debug/Display renders "***" and which does not implement Serialize. Resolved on demand via ctx.secret("NAME") (backed in v0.1 by MALLOPS_SECRET_<NAME> env vars) and excluded from config.json, cache keys, config_hash, logs, and lineage.
  • Predictor placement: in v0.1, the minimal Predictor / LoadedPredictor contract lives in mallops-std (shared by evaluate and serve; see §7 Serving) and will be promoted to mallops-core before 1.0 once validated across backends (ADR-0007).

No ML type appears in core signatures: tensors and dataframes are payload files or plugin-internal types. This is what keeps mallops library-agnostic (ADR-0004).

docs.title: 4. Execution model
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant CLI
    participant Core as Runtime
    participant Store
    participant B as Block
    CLI->>Core: run(mallops.yaml)
    Core->>Core: parse, validate config & resolved ports, topo-sort (PipelineConfig::validate)
    Core->>Core: emit RunStarted → sinks
    loop each ready node (parallel when independent)
        Core->>Core: emit BlockStarted → sinks (after job slot & cancel check)
        Core->>B: cache_policy(ctx)
        Core->>Core: cache key = hash(block id, version, config_hash, seed, input ids, extra_hash) [skipped if Uncacheable, cache: false or no_cache]
        Core->>Store: lookup(cache/<key>)
        alt cache hit (entry readable, all outputs exist)
            Core->>Core: outputs from entry, NodeSummary.cached = true, block not run
        else
            Core->>B: run(ctx, inputs) [instrumented with node span]
            B-->>Core: BlockOutcome (Produced drafts | Skipped)
            Core->>Store: put(manifest + parents, payload)
            Store-->>Core: ArtifactId
            Core->>Store: record(cache/<key>) [Succeeded only]
        end
        Core->>Core: emit ArtifactProduced (per output, incl. cache hit) + BlockFinished → sinks
    end
    Core->>Core: emit RunFinished → sinks
    Core-->>CLI: run summary
  • Scheduler: nodes in topological order start as soon as all their upstream nodes have finished, as tokio tasks in a JoinSet, bounded by a Semaphore of max_jobs permits (--jobs); spawn_blocking for heavy CPU/hashing/filesystem work (+ kill_on_drop for external child processes). Each node runs through one function (run_node: job slot → cancel check → BlockStarted → instrumented execute (Context → cache_policy → cache lookup → on a miss load inputs with store.get → block.run → commit → cache record) → ArtifactProduced per output (including cache hits) → BlockFinished), the single place where caching (#8) and lineage (#9) hook in. Once the node holds a job slot and the run is not cancelled, execute is wrapped with .instrument(info_span!("node", id, block)); the span never lives in Context. Nodes that never start (stopped by gate as Skipped or Cancelled, or cancelled before starting) emit only BlockFinished with duration: Duration::ZERO. A block that panics makes its node Failed (Error::Runtime, duration 0) and emits BlockFinished instead of crashing the run. RunStarted is emitted before scheduling any node, and RunFinished after all nodes settle and the workdir is cleaned up.
  • Cache (runtime/cache.rs): The cache is bypassed (no lookup, no record) when the node has cache: false or RuntimeConfig::no_cache is set; cache_policy is then not called. Otherwise cache_policy is asked (an error fails the node) and an Uncacheable policy bypasses it too. extra_hash must not depend on secret values (NFR-4). A hit makes the node Succeeded with NodeSummary::cached = true and outputs from the entry; the block does not run and inputs are not loaded (the node span still exists). On a miss the node runs as usual and, only if Succeeded, record stores the entry; Skipped, Failed and Cancelled are never cached. A record error, or a store error during lookup, is a tracing::warn! (the lookup error counts as a miss and the entry is rewritten), never a node failure. An unreadable or other-version entry, or one referencing an artifact missing from the store (exists), is a miss and gets overwritten.
  • Failure: a node whose block or commit fails is Status::Failed (with its error); all its descendants are Cancelled without running, with a reason naming the failed node. Independent branches still finish. Re-running resumes from cache.
  • Skipping: BlockOutcome::Skipped (e.g. a failed quality gate) marks the node Skipped; outputs it still returns are committed. A consumer with any required input from a Skipped node, or whose required upstream output was not committed, is Skipped without running, even when its other inputs succeeded (fan-in). Optional inputs without a committed artifact are absent from Inputs. A failed or cancelled parent wins over a skipped one (Cancelled).
  • Cancellation: cooperative through RuntimeConfig::cancel, the token blocks see as ctx.cancel(). Once it fires no new node starts (Cancelled, reason run cancelled); a block that returns Error::Cancelled is Cancelled with that error, not Failed. In-flight tasks are never aborted.
  • Commit (runtime/commit.rs): drafts are checked before any store.put, and all violations are reported at once as Error::Validation with paths out.<port>: unknown output port, Port::accepts_manifest mismatch (kind/format/flavor), missing required output on Produced (optional on Skipped), File/Dir payloads that do not canonicalize inside the node workdir (no .. or symlink escapes) or are not a regular file / a directory. put receives the canonical path; the window between check and put is accepted by the trust model (ADR-0007 D7). manifest.parents is replaced by the node's input ids, sorted and deduplicated. Payload content (nested symlinks, special files in a Dir) is rejected by the store during put (ArtifactStore contract); outputs of the same node committed before stay as unreferenced, immutable artifacts until a later GC.
  • Workdir: each run creates a tempfile::TempDir (prefix mallops-run-<run_id>-) in workdir_root and canonicalizes it, so ctx.workdir() (one subdirectory per node, named by its index) is absolute and canonical even for a relative or symlinked root; it is removed with spawn_blocking when the run ends.
  • Result: run returns Err only for runtime-level failures (e.g. the run workdir cannot be created); node outcomes go to the RunSummary.
  • Batch DAG only: serve is not a batch DAG node. mallops run executes blocks: and produces a package artifact; mallops serve consumes that package separately (ADR-0007).

docs.title: 5. Plugin model
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    R[Runtime] --> N[Native Rust block<br/>explicit registry in v0.1]
    R --> W[WASM component<br/>wasmtime, sandboxed]
    R --> X[External process<br/>gRPC or CLI contract]
    X --> PY[Python / R / Julia / containers]
Kind Use when Isolation Overhead Native Rust, performance critical none (trusted) zero WASM portable, untrusted, light compute strong (sandboxed, post-v0.1) low External other languages, GPUs, heavy frameworks process/container (trusted, not a sandbox) process spawn + IPC
  • Explicit registry in v0.1: BlockRegistry is an explicit, instance-local map populated via registry.register(...). mallops-cli registers the built-in core/noop block and calls mallops_std::register_std(&mut registry) (returning Result<(), Error> so duplicate block ids fail with Error::Validation). This supersedes compile-time inventory registration from ADR-0003 for v0.1 to avoid linker stripping and global test state (ADR-0007). Blocks are keyed by their spec().id, parsed as a BlockRef (grammar in SPEC §5); registering an id twice returns Error::Validation and keeps the original, and list() returns specs sorted by id.
  • External CLI contract: mallops materializes read-only inputs into the workdir, writes inputs.json (materialized paths + manifests) and config.json (never containing secrets; secrets pass only via explicit env allowlist), runs command via argv (never sh -c), and collects output files declared in outputs.json after validating every path with RelPath and rejecting symlinks. The gRPC variant adds long-lived workers and streaming. See ADR-0003.

docs.title: 6. Artifact store and lineage
docs.text:
Two kinds of "storage" exist and must not be confused:

Data storage blocks Artifact store What Persist user data to lakes, DBs, feature stores Hand artifacts from one block to the next Where in the DAG A node Every edge In the core No (mallops-std / plugins) Contract + local and memory impls Optional Yes The backend is; the mechanism is not

docs.title: 6.1 Artifact store
docs.text:
pub trait ArtifactStore: Send + Sync {
    // Immutable content-addressed artifacts (ArtifactId = canonical BLAKE3 digest)
    fn put(&self, manifest: Manifest, payload: PayloadSource<'_>) -> BoxFuture<'_, Result<ArtifactId, Error>>;
    fn get(&self, id: &ArtifactId) -> BoxFuture<'_, Result<Option<Artifact>, Error>>;
    /// Materialize the payload into `dest` (isolated writable copy locally; download + verify remotely).
    /// Never returns a writable path inside the store itself.
    fn fetch(&self, id: &ArtifactId, dest: &Path) -> BoxFuture<'_, Result<PathBuf, Error>>;
    fn verify(&self, id: &ArtifactId) -> BoxFuture<'_, Result<(), Error>>;
    fn exists(&self, id: &ArtifactId) -> BoxFuture<'_, Result<bool, Error>>;

    // Auxiliary metadata keyed by validated RelPath (cache index, lineage.json, runs/latest.json, v0.2 registry)
    fn put_meta(&self, key: &RelPath, data: &[u8]) -> BoxFuture<'_, Result<(), Error>>;
    fn get_meta(&self, key: &RelPath) -> BoxFuture<'_, Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, Error>>;
    fn list_meta(&self, prefix: &RelPath) -> BoxFuture<'_, Result<Vec<RelPath>, Error>>;
    fn delete_meta(&self, key: &RelPath) -> BoxFuture<'_, Result<(), Error>>;
}
  • Validated types: ArtifactId (strict 64 lowercase hex) and RelPath (normalized POSIX UTF-8 relative path, no .., no root prefixes) prevent path traversal across all store operations.
  • Immutability: put writes atomically (temp dir + idempotent rename), rejects symlinks and special files, and marks stored payloads read-only on LocalStore (0444 files / 0555 dirs where supported). fetch always materializes an isolated writable copy into dest so no block can mutate stored artifacts in place.
  • Core implementations: LocalStore (filesystem, default, ./.mallops, resolved by the CLI relative to the directory of mallops.yaml) and MemoryStore (ephemeral; tests and throwaway runs).
  • Optional: ObjectStore adapter over the object_store crate (S3, GCS, Azure) behind mallops-std features; anything else as a plugin.
  • What depends on it: data hand-off between nodes and processes, caching (cache/<key>.json), resume via cached re-runs, JsonSink (runs/<run-id>/lineage.json), latest run pointer (runs/latest.json), and model registry (v0.2).
  • Layout (LocalStore): artifacts/<hash>/…, meta/cache/<key>.json, meta/runs/<run-id>/lineage.json, meta/runs/latest.json, meta/registry/<model>/<version>.json (v0.2), .tmp/ (staging).
  • Latest run pointer (runs/latest.json): written by mallops run via put_meta only when every node is Succeeded, as {"v":1,"pipeline":"<name>","run":"<run-id>","outputs":{"<node>":{"<port>":"<artifact-id>"}}} (deterministic BTreeMap key ordering). Runs with Skipped nodes leave any previous runs/latest.json untouched, print latest.json not updated: <S> skipped, and exit 0; failed runs leave it untouched and exit 1.
  • Cache key (cache_key, domain-separated BLAKE3): block id, BlockSpec.version, config_hash (canonical JSON of with:, secrets stay as literal ${secret:NAME} so rotating a value does not invalidate), seed, the sorted (port, input artifact id) pairs, and extra_hash of CachePolicy::Deterministic. Node id and use: are not part of it. Entry: cache/<key-hex>.json = {"v":1,"outputs":{"<port>":"<artifact-id>"}}, stored through put_meta.

docs.title: 6.2 Lineage
docs.text:
/// Wall-clock instant; serializes as RFC 3339 UTC with millisecond precision.
pub struct Timestamp(SystemTime);

#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct HostInfo {
    pub os: String,              // std::env::consts::OS
    pub arch: String,            // std::env::consts::ARCH
    pub hostname: String,        // HOSTNAME / COMPUTERNAME env var, or "unknown"
    pub mallops_version: String, // CARGO_PKG_VERSION
}

#[non_exhaustive]
#[serde(tag = "event", rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum LineageEvent {
    #[non_exhaustive]
    RunStarted {
        run: RunId,
        timestamp: Timestamp,
        pipeline_hash: Digest,
        git_commit: Option<String>,
        host: HostInfo,
    },
    #[non_exhaustive]
    BlockStarted {
        run: RunId,
        timestamp: Timestamp,
        node: String,
        block: BlockRef,         // serialized via Display as a string (e.g. "std/train.external")
        block_version: String,
        config_hash: Digest,
        seed: Option<u64>,
        inputs: Vec<ArtifactId>,
    },
    #[non_exhaustive]
    ArtifactProduced { run: RunId, timestamp: Timestamp, node: String, artifact: ArtifactId },
    #[non_exhaustive]
    BlockFinished {
        run: RunId,
        timestamp: Timestamp,
        node: String,
        status: Status,          // snake_case: succeeded | failed | skipped | cancelled
        duration: Duration,      // serialized as `duration_ms: u64`
        cached: bool,
    },
    #[non_exhaustive]
    RunFinished { run: RunId, timestamp: Timestamp, status: Status },
}

pub trait LineageSink: Send + Sync {
    fn record<'a>(&'a self, event: &'a LineageEvent) -> BoxFuture<'a, Result<(), Error>>;
}
  • The runtime is the only producer: it alone sees the whole graph. Blocks stay unaware of lineage.
  • Document format (JsonSink): writes runs/<run-id>/lineage.json through ArtifactStore::put_meta (on LocalStore: meta/runs/<run-id>/lineage.json) as {"v":1,"run":"<run-id>","events":[...]}. Events use an internally tagged snake_case "event" field (run_started, block_started, artifact_produced, block_finished, run_finished); timestamp is RFC 3339 UTC with millisecond precision (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.mmmZ, computed from UNIX_EPOCH without an external date crate); BlockStarted.block serializes as a string; BlockFinished.duration serializes as duration_ms (u64); Status serializes in snake_case. JsonSink buffers events per run and rewrites the file on every event so it remains valid JSON after a crash, freeing the run's buffer on RunFinished.
  • Configuration (RuntimeConfig): lineage defaults to [JsonSink::new(store)] (empty Vec disables lineage, corresponding to lineage: off; mallops-cli maps off → vec![] and sink: json → JsonSink::new(store), rejecting unknown sinks in validate, run, and store verify), clock defaults to SystemTime::now (injectable for deterministic tests), host defaults to HostInfo::current() (reads HOSTNAME, falling back to COMPUTERNAME or "unknown" — env-only, no unsafe/libc), and git_commit defaults to None in the core library (mallops run populates it via best-effort git rev-parse HEAD in the directory of mallops.yaml with stderr suppressed; never spawned by validate, graph, or store verify).
  • pipeline_hash: blake3::derive_key("mallops pipeline v1", ...) over the canonical JSON array of validated nodes in topological order (id, use, BlockSpec.version, config_hash, in, seed).
  • Event order and statuses:
  • Started node: BlockStarted → one ArtifactProduced per output in NodeSummary.outputs → BlockFinished. Cache hits still emit BlockStarted, ArtifactProduced for every cached output, and BlockFinished with cached: true.
  • Node that never starts (stopped by gate, cancelled before starting, or unscheduled): only BlockFinished with duration_ms: 0 and cached: false.
  • Panicking node task: BlockStarted (already emitted) followed by BlockFinished (status: "failed", duration_ms: 0, cached: false).
  • RunFinished.status: Cancelled if RuntimeConfig::cancel fired, else Succeeded if RunSummary::is_success(), else Failed.
  • Dispatch and fault isolation: every event is sent to each sink in RuntimeConfig::lineage in order; if a sink returns Err, the runtime logs tracing::warn! and continues to the remaining sinks — a failing sink never fails the run.
  • Conformance suite: mallops_core::lineage::conformance::check_sink verifies a full event sequence covering all four Status variants and interleaved concurrent runs (supporting both read-back and write-only sinks), reusable by future sink backends (SQLite, OpenLineage, MLflow — mallops-std features or plugins in v0.2+).
  • Caching does not depend on lineage: it uses artifact hashes and cache/<key>.json in the store.

docs.title: 7. Serving
docs.text:
Serving runs outside the batch DAG via mallops serve [package-id] (using the package artifact produced by mallops run or configured in the top-level serve: section of mallops.yaml). Transports: HTTP (v0.1), gRPC (v0.2) and MQTT (v0.3, serve.transport: mqtt: request topic in, prediction topic out, see ADR-0009).

flowchart LR
    C[Client] -->|HTTP/gRPC/MQTT| S[mallops serve]
    S --> T[Preprocess transform<br/>from package]
    T --> P{Predictor by flavor}
    P --> LF[linfa]
    P --> O[ort]
    P --> TR[tract]
    P --> CA[candle]
    P --> EXT[external Python worker]
    S --> M[metrics / logs]

In v0.1, the minimal Predictor contract lives in mallops-std (shared by evaluate and serve) before promotion to mallops-core ahead of 1.0 (ADR-0007):

pub enum PredictInput {
    Json(serde_json::Value),
    Bytes { content_type: String, data: Vec<u8> },
}

pub trait Predictor: Send + Sync {
    fn flavors(&self) -> &[&str];                       // e.g. ["linfa-logistic"], ["sklearn-pickle"]
    fn executes_code(&self) -> bool;                    // true for pickle/joblib/torchscript
    fn load(&self, pkg: &Artifact, workdir: &Path) -> BoxFuture<'_, Result<Box<dyn LoadedPredictor>, Error>>;
}

pub trait LoadedPredictor: Send + Sync {
    fn predict(&self, input: PredictInput) -> BoxFuture<'_, Result<PredictInput, Error>>;
    fn predict_batch(&self, inputs: Vec<PredictInput>) -> BoxFuture<'_, Result<Vec<PredictInput>, Error>>;
}

Flavors where executes_code() is true are rejected by mallops serve unless --trust-unsafe-flavors is explicitly enabled.

docs.title: 8. Edge and federated learning (v0.4)
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    subgraph Cloud
        AGG[FL aggregator]
        REGI[Model registry]
        COL[Metrics collector]
    end
    subgraph Edge["Edge node (mallops-edge)"]
        SV[Local serving HTTP/MQTT]
        OL[Online learning DAG]
        LT[FL local training]
        BUF[Metrics buffer]
    end
    REGI -- signed model pull --> SV
    AGG -- global weights --> LT
    LT -- weight deltas only --> AGG
    SEN[Sensor] -- MQTT readings --> SV -- MQTT predictions --> CON[Consumer]
    SEN -- labelled samples --> OL -- new package if gate passes --> SV
    SV --> BUF -- push when online --> COL
    COL -- drift alert --> RT[Retrain trigger]
  • Transport: gRPC (tonic) with mTLS for the fleet control plane and FL; nodes initiate connections (NAT-friendly). MQTT for device data: serving reads requests from a topic and publishes predictions (ADR-0009).
  • Build: mallops-edge is inference-only by default (profile-edge); online and fl add only the training backends they need (ADR-0008).
  • Online learning: a finite DAG on the device produces a new immutable package from the current model (base input of incremental train blocks); serving hot-swaps only after the evaluate gate passes, keeps the previous accepted and base packages for rollback, and never mutates a served model.
  • Aggregation strategies are blocks (FedAvg default); privacy techniques plug in at the aggregator.
  • Model weights exchanged in whatever format the flavor defines; the aggregator delegates averaging to a flavor-aware plugin.

docs.title: 9. Cross-cutting concerns
docs.text: Concern Choice Errors thiserror in libraries (mallops_core::Error), anyhow only in the CLI Logging/tracing tracing (tracing-subscriber fmt on stderr in mallops-cli: WARN default, DEBUG with -v/--verbose); OpenTelemetry exporter behind a feature Config serde + serde_json + yaml_serde (yaml feature, enabled by default) + optional schemars (schema feature); ${env:NAME} interpolated at load time in with/store.path only, ${secret:NAME} stays symbolic Async tokio (rt-multi-thread in mallops-cli) CLI clap derive (exit codes: 0 success, 1 error, 2 usage error) Testing unit tests per crate, integration tests running example pipelines, insta snapshots for CLI output

docs.title: mallops — Technical Specification
docs.text: Status: Draft · Target: v0.1 · Last update: 2026-11-23

docs.title: 1. Vision
docs.text:
mallops is a modular MLOps framework written in Rust. It covers the whole machine-learning lifecycle — from data ingestion to serving, monitoring and retraining, down to edge devices with federated learning — through composable blocks.

It can be used in three ways, all backed by the same core:

Mode Who How Library Rust developers depend on mallops-core, implement Block, compose pipelines in code Plugins anyone, any language ship a block as a WASM component or as an external process speaking the mallops gRPC protocol Standalone ML engineers, ops describe a pipeline in mallops.yaml, run it with the mallops CLI, add/remove blocks without writing code

docs.title: 1.1 Design principles
docs.text:
1. Format and library agnostic. mallops never imposes a model format, a data format or an ML library. An artifact is opaque files + a manifest. ONNX, safetensors, TorchScript, pickle, GGUF, XGBoost JSON, a custom binary — all first-class.
  2. Everything is a block. Every lifecycle step, including data storage, deploy and retrain triggers, is a replaceable block with declared inputs and outputs (artifact store and lineage are core contracts acting on every edge; see ADR-0006).
  3. Small core, optional everything else. The core has no ML dependency. Standard blocks live behind Cargo feature flags.
  4. Reproducible by default. Content-addressed artifacts, recorded configs, seeds and environment.
  5. Local first, scale out later. A full pipeline runs on a laptop with zero infrastructure; the same pipeline targets object storage, remote runners and edge fleets by swapping blocks.

docs.title: 1.2 Non-goals
docs.text:
• Not a container orchestrator (it can call Kubernetes, Nomad, Docker as deploy blocks).
  • Not a deep-learning framework (it wraps burn, candle, PyTorch, scikit-learn, …).
  • Not a data warehouse or feature store (it integrates with them via blocks).
  • No GUI in v1 (a dashboard may come as a separate project).

docs.title: 2. Glossary
docs.text: Term Definition Block Unit of work with typed inputs, outputs and config. Implements the Block trait (or the plugin protocol). Stage Lifecycle category a block belongs to (ingest, preprocess, train, …). Used for docs, validation hints and CLI listing — not enforced ordering. Artifact Immutable output of a block: a set of files plus a manifest, identified by its content hash. Pipeline DAG of block instances wired by artifact references, defined in YAML or code. Run One execution of a pipeline; has an id, a lineage record and logs. Flavor Tag in a model manifest telling which loader/predictor can use it (e.g. onnx, torchscript, sklearn-pickle, gguf, custom:acme). Artifact store Internal storage through which blocks exchange artifacts. Contract in the core, backends pluggable. Not to be confused with data storage blocks. Lineage sink Pluggable destination of the lineage events emitted by the runtime (JSON file, SQLite, OpenLineage, MLflow…). Plugin Block distributed outside the mallops binary (Rust crate, WASM component, or external process). Edge node Device running mallops-edge: local serving, local metrics, optional federated training.

docs.title: 3. Functional requirements
docs.text: Each stage below lists what the standard library of blocks (mallops-std) must offer and what the core must make possible. Anything not covered can be added as a plugin.

docs.title: 3.1 Data ingestion
docs.text:
• FR-ING-1: read from local files — in v0.1, mallops-std provides std/ingest.csv (feature ingest-csv) and std/ingest.parquet (feature ingest-parquet; meta-feature ingest, enabled by default), both Stage::Ingest version 0.1.0; JSON/NDJSON and arbitrary-file ingest blocks are deferred follow-ups:
  • Both blocks reject unknown with: keys (deny_unknown_fields), run file I/O, conversion, and source hashing on tokio::task::spawn_blocking (checking ctx.cancel() between batches), resolve relative path values against the current working directory (mallops run changes into the directory of mallops.yaml, matching store.path), emit one dataset output (kind: dataset, format: parquet) backed by a single uncompressed data.parquet file with fixed footer created_by: "mallops-std" (deterministic bytes per mallops-std version) committed by the runtime (never calling store.put directly), and return CachePolicy::Deterministic { extra_hash: Some(blake3(source_file)) } (streamed BLAKE3 digest; missing source file errors) so editing the local file invalidates cached runs. Known v0.1 limitation: extra_hash is computed in cache_policy and the file is read again in run (TOCTOU); modifying a local source file concurrently during a run can associate the old cache key with the new content.
  • std/ingest.csv with: config: path (required), delimiter (ASCII char other than \n, \r, or ", default ','; invalid values fail with Error::Config), has_header (bool, default true), schema (optional list of { name, type }). Empty CSV files (0 columns) fail with empty CSV: no columns; header-only files (0 data rows) are valid. Without schema, column types are inferred across the entire file (arrow-csv may also infer Null for all-empty columns or Timestamp for ISO-8601 datetime strings — second-precision timestamps are promoted to milliseconds because Parquet has no seconds unit, so non-Arrow readers such as pandas see a timestamp rather than an integer — which lie outside the v0.1 schema: subset and therefore cannot be validated with schema: — a known v0.1 limitation). With schema, has_header: true requires the CSV header to match the declared column names in exact order (schema mismatch otherwise), while has_header: false checks that the first row has the exact declared column count (schema mismatch: expected N columns, found M) and assigns the declared names. Empty cells parse as null; non-empty unconvertible values fail the node with an error naming the source file.
  • std/ingest.parquet with: config: path (required), schema (optional list of { name, type }). Reads external Parquet files compressed with Snappy, LZ4, Gzip, or Zstd (as well as uncompressed), checks exact column names and types in order when schema is set (schema mismatch otherwise), strips source schema and field key-value metadata (e.g. pandas), and rewrites an uncompressed data.parquet so identical data with different source metadata produces identical bytes.
  • FR-ING-2: read from HTTP(S) and object stores (S3, GCS, Azure) — v0.2.
  • FR-ING-3: read from databases (PostgreSQL, SQLite) and streams (Kafka, MQTT) — v0.3+. MQTT: std/ingest.mqtt, a bounded read (max_messages, max_duration or idle_timeout) into a dataset, uncacheable, at-least-once up to the block return (ADR-0009).
  • FR-ING-4: optional schema validation accepts the v0.1 column type subset bool | int64 | float64 | string | date32 (Arrow Boolean, Int64, Float64, Utf8, Date32; nullability ignored), checked as header names (or column count when has_header: false) plus typed parsing for std/ingest.csv and exact column names and types in order for std/ingest.parquet; incremental ingestion is deferred to sources that support it.

docs.title: 3.2 Data storage
docs.text:
Two distinct concerns, deliberately kept apart (ADR-0006):

a) Data storage blocks — persisting user data to external systems is an ordinary, optional stage. - FR-STO-1: blocks that write datasets/features to object stores, data lakes (Delta, Iceberg), databases and feature stores — v0.2+; std/storage.mqtt publishes artifacts to MQTT topics — v0.3 (ADR-0009).

b) Artifact store — the internal mechanism through which blocks hand artifacts to each other. Not a block: it sits on every edge of the DAG. - FR-STO-2: the core defines the immutable ArtifactStore contract (plus an auxiliary metadata API for cache entries, run lineage records, and future registry entries) and ships two minimal implementations: local (filesystem, default) and memory (ephemeral, for tests and throwaway runs) — v0.1 (ADR-0007). - FR-STO-3: remote backends (S3, GCS, Azure, …) are optional (mallops-std features or plugins) — v0.2. - FR-STO-4: content addressing (canonical BLAKE3 over manifest and payload, excluding run provenance) — identical content is stored once; enables caching and resume. - FR-STO-5: garbage collection of artifacts unreachable from retained runs — v0.2.

docs.title: 3.3 Preprocessing (data → features)
docs.text:
• FR-PRE-1: tabular transforms (select, filter, impute, scale, encode, split) on Arrow data — v0.1.
  • FR-PRE-2: user-defined transforms (Rust closure, WASM, external process).
  • FR-PRE-3: fitted transforms are themselves artifacts, so serving reuses the exact same preprocessing.

docs.title: 3.4 Training
docs.text:
• FR-TRN-1: native Rust training (linfa for classic ML) — v0.1.
  • FR-TRN-2: deep learning via burn/candle — v0.3.
  • FR-TRN-3: external trainer: run any command/container (Python, R, Julia…) that reads input artifacts and writes outputs into a mallops-managed workspace directory — v0.1. This is how PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn, XGBoost are supported without Rust bindings.
  • FR-TRN-4: hyperparameters, seed and environment recorded in the run lineage.

docs.title: 3.5 Model engineering
docs.text:
• FR-ENG-1: hyperparameter search (grid, random; Bayesian as plugin) as a block that fans out training sub-runs — v0.2.
  • FR-ENG-2: post-training transforms as blocks: quantization, pruning, format conversion (e.g. torch → onnx) — delegated to the relevant tool.

docs.title: 3.6 Model evaluation
docs.text:
• FR-EVL-1: standard metrics (accuracy, precision/recall/F1, ROC-AUC, RMSE, MAE, R²) — v0.1.
  • FR-EVL-2: quality gates: a pipeline can fail or branch when a metric is below a threshold or worse than the current production model.
  • FR-EVL-3: custom metrics via plugins.

docs.title: 3.7 Model packaging
docs.text:
• FR-PKG-1: package = model artifact + preprocessing transform artifacts + manifest (flavor, io_schema, requirements) — v0.1.
  • FR-PKG-2: optional OCI image output for serving — v0.2.
  • FR-PKG-3: artifact signing (Sigstore/cosign or ed25519) — v0.3.

docs.title: 3.8 Model versioning
docs.text:
• FR-VER-1: model registry backed by the artifact store: name → versions → stages (staging, production, archived) — v0.2.
  • FR-VER-2: every version links to the run lineage that produced it (data hashes, code version, config).

docs.title: 3.9 Deploy
docs.text:
• FR-DEP-1: deploy targets as blocks: local process, Docker, Kubernetes manifest, SSH host, edge fleet — v0.2+.
  • FR-DEP-2: strategies: replace, canary, shadow — v0.3.
  • FR-DEP-3: rollback to a previous registry version in one command.

docs.title: 3.10 Model serving
docs.text:
• FR-SRV-1: HTTP/JSON inference server (mallops serve [package-id]) running outside the batch DAG, consuming a package artifact produced by mallops run — v0.1 (ADR-0007).
  • FR-SRV-2: gRPC endpoint, batching, health/readiness probes — v0.2.
  • FR-SRV-4: MQTT transport (serve.transport: mqtt): read requests from a topic, predict, publish to a response topic; at-least-once, acknowledged after the prediction is published — v0.3 (ADR-0009).
  • FR-SRV-3: backend-agnostic: the server dispatches to a Predictor chosen by the package flavor (linfa, external Python process in v0.1; ort, tract, candle, burn, llama.cpp…). In v0.1 the minimal Predictor contract lives in mallops-std (shared by evaluate and serve) and is promoted to mallops-core before 1.0 (ADR-0007).

docs.title: 3.11 Monitoring and logging
docs.text:
• FR-MON-1: structured logs (tracing) for every run and every request — v0.1.
  • FR-MON-2: Prometheus metrics and OpenTelemetry traces — v0.3.
  • FR-MON-3: data/prediction drift detection (PSI, KS test) as blocks — v0.3.

docs.title: 3.12 Retrain
docs.text:
• FR-RET-1: triggers as blocks: schedule (cron), drift alert, new data, manual — v0.3.
  • FR-RET-2: a trigger starts a pipeline run; evaluation gates decide promotion.

docs.title: 3.13 Edge
docs.text:
• FR-EDG-1: mallops-edge agent: single static binary, cross-compiled for aarch64/armv7/x86_64, inference-only by default (profile-edge of mallops-std, which includes HTTP and MQTT serving) — v0.4 (ADR-0008).
  • FR-EDG-2: local serving with any Predictor backend, offline-capable.
  • FR-EDG-3: distributed monitoring: nodes buffer metrics/drift stats locally and push them when connected.
  • FR-EDG-4: federated learning: central aggregator (FedAvg, FedProx as plugin), nodes train locally, only model updates leave the device; optional secure aggregation and differential privacy as plugins.
  • FR-EDG-5: fleet deploy: pull-based model updates with signature verification.
  • FR-EDG-6: on-device online learning (online feature): a finite DAG (ingest new labelled samples, e.g. from MQTT → train from the current model via an optional base input → evaluate gate → package) produces a new immutable package; serving hot-swaps to it only if the gate passes, with rollback and bounded retention (ADR-0008).

docs.title: 3.14 Lineage
docs.text:
• FR-LIN-1: the runtime emits lineage events (RunStarted, BlockStarted, ArtifactProduced, BlockFinished, RunFinished) with RFC 3339 UTC millisecond timestamps (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.mmmZ, computed from SystemTime without an external date crate) — v0.1. RunStarted carries pipeline_hash (domain-separated BLAKE3 "mallops pipeline v1" over canonical JSON of the topologically ordered nodes: id, use, BlockSpec.version, config_hash, in, seed), git_commit (None in the core library; populated by mallops-cli), and host (os, arch, hostname from HOSTNAME/COMPUTERNAME or "unknown", mallops_version). Each started node emits BlockStarted (block string, block_version, config_hash, seed, inputs), one ArtifactProduced per output (including cache hits), and BlockFinished (status, duration_ms, cached: true on cache hits). Nodes that never start (Skipped or Cancelled before execution) emit only BlockFinished with duration_ms: 0. RunFinished reports Cancelled if the run was cancelled, else Succeeded if RunSummary::is_success(), else Failed.
  • FR-LIN-2: events go to pluggable LineageSinks; the core ships JsonSink (default in RuntimeConfig::new), writing runs/<run-id>/lineage.json = {"v":1,"run":"<run-id>","events":[...]} (events internally tagged with "event" in snake_case) via ArtifactStore::put_meta, rewritten on every event so the file stays valid JSON after a crash — v0.1. mallops_core::lineage::conformance::check_sink provides a shared conformance suite reusable by future sinks. SQLite, OpenLineage and MLflow sinks are optional — v0.2+.
  • FR-LIN-3: multiple sinks can be active at once via RuntimeConfig::lineage (YAML lineage: mapping lives in mallops-cli); an empty sink list (lineage: off) disables lineage entirely while caching still works (it relies on artifact hashes and cache/<key>.json, not on lineage). A sink returning Err logs a tracing::warn! and never fails the run.
  • FR-LIN-4: secrets are never written to any sink, log, workdir, or store (verified by lineage_anti_leak_*).

docs.title: 4. Non-functional requirements
docs.text: Id Requirement NFR-1 Performance Core overhead per block < 5 ms (median on MemoryStore, checked by the ignored test runtime_nfr1_block_overhead); independent branches run in parallel. NFR-2 Reproducibility Same config + same input hashes + same seed ⇒ same artifact hashes for deterministic blocks; unchanged nodes are not re-executed: their outputs are served from the content-hash cache (NodeSummary.cached), cache: false or --no-cache (RuntimeConfig::no_cache) bypass it. NFR-3 Portability Linux, macOS, Windows; x86_64 and aarch64. Edge targets armv7. NFR-4 Security Secrets only via redacted ${secret:NAME} references (never written to config.json, cache keys, config_hash, logs, workdir, store, or lineage; checked by lineage_anti_leak_*); mallops.yaml, native blocks, and external processes are trusted code — sandboxing applies only to WASM plugins; unsafe code-executing model flavors require explicit opt-in at serve time; signed artifacts from v0.3. NFR-5 Observability Every run emits structured tracing logs (per-node node span, warnings on cache or lineage sink errors) and, unless lineage: off (RuntimeConfig::lineage empty), a lineage record (runs/<run-id>/lineage.json by default, rewritten incrementally per event). NFR-6 Stability Semantic versioning; public API of mallops-core frozen at 1.0 (#[non_exhaustive] on extensible public types). MSRV documented and tested in CI. NFR-7 Footprint mallops-core compiles without any ML, cloud-SDK, object_store, database, or HTTP/gRPC dependency; dependencies are restricted to the explicit allowlist (tokio, serde, serde_json, blake3, tracing, thiserror, ulid, tempfile) plus feature-gated yaml (yaml_serde, default) and schema (schemars, optional) (ADR-0007).

docs.title: 4.1 Trust model
docs.text:
mallops enforces explicit trust boundaries (ADR-0007):

  • Pipeline definitions (mallops.yaml) are trusted code. Running mallops run is equivalent to executing a build script: native blocks run in-process, external blocks run arbitrary configured commands (command:), and mallops run spawns git rev-parse HEAD (best-effort, in the directory of mallops.yaml, stderr discarded; failure yields None) to record RunStarted.git_commit. By contrast, mallops validate and mallops graph never execute user code, spawn external processes (not even git), or create the artifact store directory. mallops store verify likewise never runs blocks or spawns external processes.
  • Plugin isolation boundaries. Only WASM component plugins (post-v0.1) execute inside a capability-restricted sandbox. Native Rust blocks have no isolation; external CLI and gRPC blocks run as host processes. In v0.1, external CLI blocks execute via argv (never through a shell), with an explicit allowlisted environment and an isolated workdir, but this is process hygiene rather than a security sandbox.
  • Model flavor deserialization. Formats such as pickle, joblib, sklearn-pickle, and torchscript execute arbitrary code when loaded. Predictor implementations declare executes_code(&self) -> bool, and mallops serve refuses to load code-executing flavors unless --trust-unsafe-flavors is explicitly passed. Prefer non-executing formats (onnx, safetensors, skops) and, from v0.3, cryptographically signed packages.
  • Secrets. ${secret:NAME} references are resolved on demand through a SecretProvider (MALLOPS_SECRET_<NAME> environment variable in v0.1) into an opaque Secret newtype whose Debug/Display output is redacted ("***") and which does not implement Serialize. Secrets never enter Context.config, config.json, cache keys, config_hash, logs, or lineage sinks.
  • Store integrity. ArtifactId (strict 64 lowercase hex chars) and RelPath (relative POSIX UTF-8 path with no .. or root prefixes) are strictly validated. ArtifactStore rejects symlinks and special files, stores payloads read-only on LocalStore, and materializes copies on fetch so blocks can never mutate stored artifacts in place.

docs.title: 5. Pipeline definition (mallops.yaml)
docs.text:
version: 1
name: churn-classifier

store:                   # artifact store (optional, this is the default)
  kind: local            # local | memory | s3 | gcs | azure | plugin:<name>
  path: ./.mallops

lineage:                 # optional; default is [{ sink: json }]
  - sink: json
  - sink: openlineage
    with: { url: "${env:OPENLINEAGE_URL}" }
  # lineage: off         # disable completely

blocks:
  raw:
    use: std/ingest.csv
    with:
      path: data/customers.csv

  features:
    use: std/preprocess.tabular
    in: { data: raw.dataset }
    with:
      target: churned
      steps:
        - impute: { strategy: median }
        - scale: { method: standard }
        - split: { test: 0.2, seed: 42 }

  model:
    use: std/train.external            # any language, any library
    in: { train: features.train }
    with:
      command: ["python", "train.py"]
      flavor: sklearn-pickle
      params: { n_estimators: 200 }

  eval:
    use: std/evaluate.classification
    in: { model: model.model, test: features.test }
    with:
      gate: { metric: f1, min: 0.80 }

  package:
    use: std/package
    in: { model: model.model, preprocess: features.transform, metrics: eval.metrics }

serve:                   # optional serving config read by `mallops serve` (not a DAG node)
  package: package.package
  host: 127.0.0.1
  port: 8080

Rules: - blocks: defines the finite batch DAG executed by mallops run. Long-running serving lives in the optional top-level serve: section (read by mallops serve, never started by mallops run). - use references a block by namespace/name, where name is stage[.variant] (e.g. std/ingest.csv, std/package). Each segment starts with [a-z0-9] and contains only [a-z0-9_-]; anything else fails as a malformed block reference (std/… built-in in v0.1; plugin/…, wasm:path.wasm, and grpc:host:port are reserved for post-v0.1 plugin runtimes and fail with a clear error in v0.1). - in wires named inputs to <block>.<output> (split at the first .); this defines the DAG. Cycles and self-loops are rejected. - with is block-specific config, validated by Block::validate_config (using serde in v0.1; optional JSON Schema validation behind the schema-validate feature). Each block also supports cache: false to bypass caching for that node and an optional seed: (u64) for deterministic blocks; the seed is part of the cache key, so changing it re-executes the node. The run-level --no-cache (RuntimeConfig::no_cache) bypasses the cache for every node. - Validation (PipelineConfig::validate, behind mallops validate) runs in one pass, never calls Block::run, and reports every problem at once as Error::Validation(Vec<ValidationError>), each with a dotted path: blocks.<id>.use (unknown block, or a Stage::Serve block, which is not a DAG node), blocks.<id>.in.<port> (malformed reference, unknown upstream node or output port, undeclared input port, kind/format/flavor mismatch, required input not connected), blocks.<id>.with[.<sub>] (errors of Block::validate_config and Block::resolve_ports, prefixed with blocks.<id>.with), blocks.<id> (one error per cycle, on its first node by id, listing the nodes) and serve.package (not <node>.<output>, unknown node or output, or kind other than package). A node whose block is unknown, is a Stage::Serve block, or whose with: fails validate_config or resolve_ports is unresolved: checks that need its ports (declared input ports, required inputs, output ports, kind/format/flavor compatibility of the edges touching it, serve.package pointing at it) are skipped, so one root cause yields one error. When validate_config fails, resolve_ports is not called. Nodes of the validated pipeline are in topological order, ties broken by node id. - Execution (Runtime::run, behind mallops run) runs nodes of the validated pipeline as soon as all their upstream nodes have finished, at most --jobs (RuntimeConfig::max_jobs, 0 counts as 1) blocks at a time, and returns a RunSummary with one NodeSummary per node: status (Succeeded, Failed, Skipped, Cancelled), duration, committed output ids, cached (outputs served from the cache), and a skip/cancel reason or the error. Node outcomes never make run return Err; only runtime failures do (for example, the run workdir cannot be created). Rules: - A node whose block or output commit fails is Failed; all its descendants are Cancelled without running, with a reason naming the failed node. Independent branches finish. - BlockOutcome::Skipped marks the node Skipped (outputs it still returns are committed). A consumer is Skipped without running when any required input comes from a Skipped node or was not committed, even if its other inputs succeeded (fan-in). An optional input without a committed artifact is simply absent. If a node has both a failed/cancelled and a skipped parent, it is Cancelled. - Cancellation is cooperative: once the run's CancelToken fires, no new node starts (Cancelled, reason run cancelled); a running block that returns Error::Cancelled is Cancelled (not Failed). Nothing is aborted forcibly. - Output drafts are validated before any store.put (errors at out.<port>): every draft names a declared output port and satisfies its kind/format/flavor; a Produced outcome provides every required output; File/Dir payloads canonicalize inside the node workdir to a regular file / a directory, and the canonical path is what the store receives. The runtime sets parents to the node's input ids (sorted, deduplicated). Payload content (nested symlinks, special files inside a Dir) is checked by the store during put; if that fails the node is Failed, and outputs of the same node committed before stay in the store as unreferenced artifacts (immutable, harmless, removed by a later GC). - Cache (NFR-2): after the node gets its job slot, the cache is bypassed when cache: false is set or no_cache is on (Block::cache_policy is then not called); otherwise Block::cache_policy is consulted (an error fails the node; extra_hash must not depend on secrets) and Uncacheable bypasses it too. Otherwise a hit (all recorded output artifacts still in the store) marks the node Succeeded with cached: true, its outputs taken from the entry, and the block is not run; a miss runs it. Only Succeeded nodes are cached (Skipped, Failed, Cancelled always re-run). Failing to write the entry, or a store error while reading it (treated as a miss), is a warning, the node stays Succeeded. A rerun re-executes every node that did not succeed, plus the descendants whose inputs changed. - Each run gets a temporary workdir under RuntimeConfig::workdir_root (which may be relative) with one subdirectory per node; ctx.workdir() is always absolute and canonical. The run workdir is removed when the run ends. - Values may reference environment variables ${env:NAME} (resolved into config and included in config_hash; NAME is [A-Za-z0-9_]+; interpolated only in string values of each block's with, of lineage sink with, and in store.path, never in keys, in, seed or elsewhere; replaced text is not re-scanned; no escape syntax; a missing variable is an error naming the file and the block, sink or store.path) and secrets ${secret:NAME} (same NAME charset, validated at load; kept literally in the config, never resolved at load time; resolved on demand via MALLOPS_SECRET_<NAME> in v0.1 into a redacted Secret, never written to config.json, cache keys, logs, or lineage). - Unknown keys are rejected (deny_unknown_fields); lineage accepts only off or a list of sinks; version must be 1; duplicate block ids (or in ports) are rejected. Syntax and schema errors are reported as <file>:<line>:<column>: <message>. - Store and lineage backend mapping in the v0.1 CLI (check_backends, enforced by validate, run, and store verify): - store.kind accepts local (LocalStore at <yaml-dir>/<store.path>, where <yaml-dir> is the parent directory of the mallops.yaml path, defaulting to . when empty) and memory (MemoryStore). Any other store.kind fails with an error. - lineage: off disables lineage (RuntimeConfig::lineage = vec![]); otherwise every configured sink must have sink: json (JsonSink on the configured store). Any other sink name fails with an error. - Built-in blocks in mallops-cli: core/noop (version 1.0.0, Stage::Custom, optional input in: blob, output out: blob with format: noop and empty payload; test affordances fail: "<message>" and skip: "<reason>" in with:) plus all feature-enabled standard blocks registered via mallops_std::register_std(&mut registry) (in v0.1 so far: std/ingest.csv, std/ingest.parquet). - Latest run pointer (runs/latest.json): after mallops run, if and only if every node is Succeeded, the CLI writes runs/latest.json via ArtifactStore::put_meta (meta/runs/latest.json on LocalStore) as {"v":1,"pipeline":"<name>","run":"<run-id>","outputs":{"<node>":{"<port>":"<artifact-id>"}}} (deterministic key order via BTreeMap), so mallops serve can resolve serve.package without an explicit id. If any node is Skipped (with no failed/cancelled nodes), mallops run leaves any previous runs/latest.json unchanged, prints latest.json not updated: <S> skipped, and exits 0. A failed run leaves any previous runs/latest.json unchanged and exits 1 (error: run failed). - A JSON Schema for mallops.yaml can be generated via the optional schema feature (schemars) for editor completion.

docs.title: 5.1 CLI (mallops)
docs.text:
Global flags: --version (-V), -v / --verbose (stderr tracing logs at DEBUG instead of WARN), and -f / --file <PATH> (default mallops.yaml).

Exit codes: 0 on success, 1 on configuration, validation, runtime, or store verification error, 2 on CLI argument/usage error (clap).

Command Behavior mallops init [DIR] Writes a minimal runnable mallops.yaml (two core/noop nodes, hello → world) into DIR (default ., creating missing parent directories); fails if mallops.yaml already exists. mallops validate Parses and validates mallops.yaml (including serve: if present) and checks supported store/lineage backends without executing blocks or spawning processes. Prints ok: <name> (<N> blocks) on stdout, or every validation error (error: <path>: <message>) on stderr. mallops run [--jobs N] [--no-cache] Validates and executes the batch DAG (blocks: only; ignores serve:). Changes the working directory to the directory of mallops.yaml so relative paths in block configs (such as std/ingest.* path) resolve against the pipeline directory, matching store.path. --jobs N overrides RuntimeConfig::max_jobs (default: available parallelism; 0 counts as 1); --no-cache bypasses the cache. Populates git_commit via best-effort git rev-parse HEAD in the mallops.yaml directory. Prints one line per node in topological order (<node> <status>[ (cached)] <ms>ms[: <reason/error>]) followed by run <run-id>: <E> executed, <C> cached, <F> failed, <S> skipped, <X> cancelled (executed = non-cached Succeeded). Writes runs/latest.json only when every node is Succeeded (if any node is Skipped, prints latest.json not updated: <S> skipped and exits 0); exits 1 on failure. mallops graph [--format mermaid\|dot] Prints the validated DAG in topological order as Mermaid (flowchart TD, default) or Graphviz DOT (digraph), with edges labeled by input port name, without executing blocks or spawning processes. mallops blocks list Prints registered blocks (ID, VERSION, STAGE, INPUTS, OUTPUTS; optional inputs suffixed with ?, empty port list shown as -), sorted by block id. mallops store verify <ID> Parses <ID> as an ArtifactId, checks backends, opens the configured store (for kind: local, fails with store not found: <path> without creating it if absent), and calls ArtifactStore::verify. Prints ok: <id> on stdout on success; exits 1 on invalid id, missing store/artifact, or corruption/tampering.

docs.title: 6. Artifact contract
docs.text:
<store>/artifacts/<blake3-hash>/
├── manifest.json
└── payload/…          # any files, opaque to the core

{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "kind": "model",
  "format": "pickle",
  "flavor": "sklearn-pickle",
  "io_schema": { "inputs": [{"name": "age", "dtype": "f64"}], "outputs": [{"name": "churned", "dtype": "f64"}] },
  "metadata": { "framework": "scikit-learn", "framework_version": "1.6.0" },
  "parents": ["<hash>", "<hash>"]
}

Per-run provenance (run, node) is not part of manifest.json; it is recorded in LineageEvent::ArtifactProduced so identical deterministic runs produce identical ArtifactIds (ADR-0007). Cryptographic signatures (FR-PKG-3, v0.3) are stored alongside artifacts rather than inside manifest.json.

Canonical ArtifactId encoding (v1): 1. Initialize a BLAKE3 keyed hasher with blake3::derive_key("mallops artifact v1"). 2. Serialize Manifest as canonical compact JSON (object keys sorted by UTF-8 byte order, numbers in serde_json format — not RFC 8785 — io_schema: null omitted as absent, and parents sorted lexicographically and deduplicated) and hash u64::to_le_bytes(len) || manifest_json_bytes. 3. Collect all payload files via validated RelPath (relative UTF-8 POSIX paths with / separators, no .., no symlinks) sorted bytewise; hash u64::to_le_bytes(file_count) followed by len(path) || path || len(content) || blake3(content) for each file (all lengths as u64 little-endian). 4. Encode the 32-byte digest as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

kind Typical format values Notes dataset parquet, arrow-ipc, csv, json, images, tfrecord, any Arrow/Parquet is the interchange default for std blocks only (ADR-0002): std/ingest.* emit format: parquet with a single uncompressed payload/data.parquet file (created_by: "mallops-std", deterministic per mallops-std version, source schema metadata stripped) features as dataset preprocessed feature splits transform json, bin, pickle, any fitted preprocessor (scaler, imputer, encoder…) reused by package and serve model onnx, safetensors, torchscript, pickle, joblib, gguf, xgboost-json, savedmodel, any flavor selects the predictor metrics json key → number map + optional plots package dir, oci model + transforms + manifest blob any escape hatch

Model flavor code-execution safety:

Flavor / format Executes code on load? Serving default onnx, safetensors, linfa-*, xgboost-json, gguf, skops No Allowed pickle, joblib, sklearn-pickle, torchscript Yes Refused unless --trust-unsafe-flavors

Inputs and outputs of blocks declare the accepted kind and optionally accepted formats / flavors; mallops validate checks compatibility before running (using Block::resolve_ports when ports depend on with: config); an output is wired into an input only if its kind is equal and every format/flavor it may produce is accepted (an empty accepted list means any; an unconstrained output, i.e. an empty list, does not satisfy a constrained input). Error paths are listed in §5.

docs.title: 7. Roadmap
docs.text: Version Scope v0.1 mallops-core (Block trait, canonical artifacts, immutable ArtifactStore + local/memory + auxiliary metadata, explicit BlockRegistry, lineage events + JSON sink, DAG runtime, YAML), CLI (init, validate, run, graph, blocks list, store verify, serve), mallops-std (Predictor contract, ingest csv/parquet, preprocess tabular, train linfa + external, evaluate classification/regression, package, HTTP serving) v0.2 remote store backends, SQLite/OpenLineage/MLflow lineage sinks, data storage blocks, model registry & versioning, hyperparameter search, deploy local/docker, gRPC serving, OCI packaging v0.3 monitoring (Prometheus/OTel), drift detection, retrain triggers, DL training (burn/candle), signing, canary/shadow deploy, MQTT ingest/publish blocks and MQTT serving transport v0.4 mallops-edge (edge build profiles), on-device online learning, federated learning, fleet deploy, distributed monitoring v1.0 stable public API, plugin protocol v1 frozen

docs.title: 8. Open questions
docs.text:
• Plugin discovery/distribution: crates.io-style index vs. OCI registry for WASM/gRPC plugins.
  • Python SDK for writing external blocks (thin package implementing the protocol) — likely v0.2.
  • Which lineage sink becomes the recommended default for querying (SQLite vs. OpenLineage backend) once registries need search.

  • A hotfix/* branch must bump the patch version in Cargo.toml and update CHANGELOG.md.

docs.title: Commits and PR titles
docs.text: PRs are squash-merged, so the PR title becomes the commit and must follow Conventional Commits: feat(core): add artifact store, fix(cli): …, docs: …, refactor: …, test: …, ci: …, build: …, chore: …. Breaking changes: feat!: … or a BREAKING CHANGE: footer.

docs.title: Developer Certificate of Origin (DCO)
docs.text:
Every commit must be signed off, certifying that you wrote it or otherwise have the right to submit it under the project license, as stated in the Developer Certificate of Origin. The sign-off is a trailer matching the commit author:

Signed-off-by: Jane Doe <jane@example.com>

Add it with git commit -s. To fix commits already in a PR:

git rebase --signoff origin/dev        # adds the trailer to every commit of the branch
git push --force-with-lease

The dco CI job blocks PRs with unsigned commits and rejects merge commits in feature PRs (rebase onto dev instead; verified dependabot[bot]/github-actions[bot] commits and verified GitHub merge commits in release/back-merge PRs are exempt). Squash merges keep all trailers in the final commit.

docs.title: Local checks
docs.text:
cargo fmt --all
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --all-features

CI also runs, and ci-ok requires:

  • Coverage: cargo llvm-cov --workspace --all-features --fail-under-lines 85 (install with cargo install cargo-llvm-cov).
  • SAST: CodeQL (security-and-quality) on Rust and on the workflows; any error or warning fails the PR. Alerts are in the Security tab.
  • SCA: cargo deny check on the whole dependency tree (advisories, licenses, sources), plus GitHub dependency review on the dependencies a PR adds or updates.
  • Workflow security: zizmor on .github/ (uvx zizmor .; config in .github/zizmor.yml).

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
The site is built with MkDocs Material from docs/ and published on GitHub Pages, versioned with mike: /dev/ follows the dev branch, /X.Y/ is published at each release, /latest/ points to the newest stable one.

pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
mkdocs serve          # live preview on http://127.0.0.1:8000
mkdocs build --strict # what CI runs on PRs

The Rust API reference is generated by rustdoc and hosted on docs.rs.

docs.title: Releasing (maintainers)
docs.text:
1. Actions → Start release → choose patch|minor|major. This opens release/X.Y.Z → main and publishes vX.Y.Z-beta.1.
  2. Test the beta; push fixes to the release branch (each push = new beta).
  3. Merge the PR with Create a merge commit. The tag, GitHub Release, binaries and crates.io publish happen automatically.
  4. Merge the auto-opened back-merge PR into dev (merge commit).

Required secrets: RELEASE_TOKEN (repository secret, fine-grained PAT or GitHub App token with contents + pull-requests write, so bot-created branches/PRs trigger CI) and CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN (in the release environment, for crates.io).
