docs.title: Architecture Decision Records
docs.text:
Format: MADR light. One decision per file, numbered, never edited after acceptance — supersede with a new ADR instead.

# Title Status 0001 Modular Cargo workspace Accepted 0002 Arrow/Parquet as default (not mandatory) data interchange Accepted 0003 Plugins via WASM components and external processes Accepted 0004 Format-agnostic artifacts with flavors Accepted 0005 GitFlow branching and automated releases Accepted 0006 Artifact store and lineage: contracts in the core, implementations pluggable Accepted 0007 Core contracts revision before v0.1 implementation Accepted 0008 Edge build profiles and on-device online learning Accepted 0009 MQTT blocks and MQTT serving transport Accepted

docs.title: 0001 — Modular Cargo workspace
docs.text: • Status: Accepted · 2026-11-20

docs.title: Context
docs.text: mallops must be usable as a library, with plugins, or standalone. Users should pay (compile time, binary size, dependencies) only for the blocks they use.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: A Cargo workspace with a small number of crates: mallops-core (no ML deps), mallops-std (standard blocks, each behind a feature flag), mallops-cli, and later mallops-edge. Crates are created only when they have code.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• cargo add mallops-std --features train-linfa,serve-http gives exactly what is needed.
  • Fewer crates = simpler releases. If mallops-std grows too heavy, per-stage crates can be split out without breaking users (re-exports).

docs.title: 0002 — Arrow/Parquet as default (not mandatory) data interchange
docs.text: • Status: Accepted · 2026-11-20

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Standard blocks need a common tabular representation to interoperate. At the same time mallops must not lock users into one data format.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Standard tabular blocks exchange data as Parquet files (on disk) and Arrow RecordBatch (in memory). This is a convention of mallops-std, not of the core: a dataset artifact can have any format, and blocks declare which formats they accept.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Zero-copy interop with Polars, DataFusion, DuckDB, pandas/pyarrow in external blocks.
  • Non-tabular data (images, audio, text corpora) flows as plain files with a declared format.
  • Format conversion is an explicit block, never implicit.

docs.title: 0003 — Plugins via WASM components and external processes
docs.text: • Status: Accepted · 2026-11-20

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Users need to add blocks without recompiling mallops, often in languages other than Rust (Python dominates ML). Rust has no stable ABI, so dylib plugins break across compiler versions.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Three plugin kinds, all exposed to the runtime through the same Block trait: 1. Native: Rust crates registered at compile time (inventory). 2. WASM components (wasmtime, WIT interface) for portable, sandboxed blocks. 3. External processes via a file-based CLI contract (inputs.json/config.json → outputs.json) and, for long-lived workers, a gRPC protocol.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Any language works through the external contract; a thin Python SDK is planned.
  • No dylib loading, no ABI issues.
  • The WIT and protobuf definitions become public API and are versioned with the core.

docs.title: 0004 — Format-agnostic artifacts with flavors
docs.text: • Status: Accepted · 2026-11-20

docs.title: Context
docs.text: ML teams use many model formats (ONNX, safetensors, TorchScript, pickle/joblib, GGUF, XGBoost JSON, SavedModel, custom). Picking one (e.g. ONNX) would exclude models that cannot be converted and force lossy conversions.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: An artifact is opaque payload files plus a manifest.json with kind, format, flavor and free-form metadata. The core never reads payloads. Model consumers (serving, evaluation, edge) select an implementation of the Predictor trait by flavor. Backends (ort, tract, candle, burn, linfa, llama.cpp, external Python workers…) are all equal plugins.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Any model, any library, any language.
  • Validation is limited to declared metadata; a block that receives an unsupported flavor fails early at mallops validate.
  • Conversions (e.g. torch → onnx) are explicit model-engineering blocks.

docs.title: 0005 — GitFlow branching and automated releases
docs.text: • Status: Accepted · 2026-11-20

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The project needs a clear contribution flow, stable releases, and a way to ship pre-releases for testing.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• main: only released code; every commit is a tag vX.Y.Z.
  • dev: default branch, integration of feature/* and fix/* via PR.
  • release/X.Y.Z: cut from dev by the Start release workflow; every push publishes a GitHub pre-release vX.Y.Z-beta.N. It acts as the beta channel, so no extra long-lived beta branch.
  • hotfix/*: from main, merged back to main and dev.
  • Conventional Commits enforced on PR titles (squash merge); changelog generated by git-cliff.
  • Merge of a release/hotfix PR into main tags, creates the GitHub Release with binaries, publishes crates, and opens a back-merge PR into dev.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• One click to start a release, zero manual tagging.
  • Squash merges keep history linear and changelog accurate.

docs.title: 0006 — Artifact store and lineage: contracts in the core, implementations pluggable
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted · 2026-11-21
  • Refines: 0001

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The first draft put the artifact store (on top of object_store) and the lineage store inside mallops-core. That contradicts the "small core, optional everything else" principle and drags cloud dependencies into every build.

Two alternatives were considered: 1. Make them blocks. Rejected: blocks are nodes of the DAG, while store and lineage act on every edge. If storage were an optional node, the runtime could not hand data from A to B, and caching/resume would depend on the user remembering to add it. Lineage needs the whole graph, which only the runtime sees; a block would have to rebuild it. 2. Keep full implementations in the core. Rejected: forces object_store and a lineage backend on every user.

The draft also mixed two different things: the data storage lifecycle stage (persisting user data) and the internal artifact store.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• The core defines the contracts: ArtifactStore and LineageSink traits, plus the LineageEvent type emitted by the runtime.
  • The core ships only minimal, dependency-free implementations: LocalStore (filesystem, default), MemoryStore (ephemeral), JsonSink (one lineage.json per run).
  • Remote stores (S3, GCS, Azure via object_store) and other lineage sinks (SQLite, OpenLineage, MLflow) are mallops-std features or plugins.
  • Lineage supports zero or more sinks; lineage: off disables it. Sink failures are warnings, never run failures.
  • "Data storage" as a lifecycle stage is an ordinary optional block that writes user data to external systems; it is unrelated to the artifact store.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• mallops-core has no cloud or database dependency.
  • Caching, resume and data hand-off always work, because the store mechanism cannot be removed — only its backend swapped.
  • Caching relies on artifact hashes, not lineage, so disabling lineage loses audit history but not performance.
  • ArtifactStore, LineageSink and LineageEvent become public API and must stay stable from 1.0.

docs.title: 0007 — Core contracts revision before v0.1 implementation
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted · 2026-11-21
  • Partially supersedes: 0003 (compile-time inventory registration; plugin isolation table), 0004 (Predictor placement in v0.1; manifest fields)
  • Refines: 0001, 0006

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
A pre-implementation design review of SPEC.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, and the existing ADRs uncovered eight structural defects in mallops-core contracts that would cause cascading breaking changes as soon as v0.1 development starts:

  1. Including produced_by.run inside the hashed Manifest breaks content addressing, deduplication, and caching; the hash framing itself was unspecified.
  2. NFR-7 restricted mallops-core to four crates while core features require additional infrastructure crates, serde_yaml is archived upstream, and schemars::Schema leaked into public signatures.
  3. ArtifactStore lacked real immutability on LocalStore, validated ID/path types, and an API for auxiliary metadata (cache index, lineage.json, model registry).
  4. Core trait and struct signatures (Block, BlockSpec, Context, Manifest, LineageEvent, Error) were missing versioning, skip outcomes, cancellation, secret isolation, runtime-managed output commits, #[non_exhaustive], ArtifactKind::Transform, and an unambiguous I/O schema field name.
  5. serve was modeled both as a batch DAG node and as a standalone CLI command.
  6. Predictor was placed in mallops-core before being validated against real backends and out of dependency order with evaluate.
  7. No explicit trust model existed for executable YAML pipelines, code-executing model flavors, or actual plugin isolation boundaries.
  8. Compile-time inventory registration is fragile under LTO/cross-compilation, breaks test isolation, and adds unnecessary complexity for v0.1.

docs.title: D1 — Canonical ArtifactId encoding without produced_by
docs.text:
Decision: - Remove produced_by (and all run-specific or timestamp fields) from the content-addressed Manifest. Per-run provenance (run, node, artifact) is recorded exclusively in LineageEvent::ArtifactProduced. - Define a canonical, cross-platform encoding for ArtifactId using BLAKE3 with domain separation (blake3::derive_key("mallops artifact v1")): 1. Serialize the canonical Manifest (schema_version, kind, format, flavor, io_schema, parents, metadata) as canonical JSON with sorted object keys (BTreeMap / RFC 8785) and parents sorted lexicographically by ArtifactId; feed u64::to_le_bytes(manifest_bytes.len()) || manifest_bytes. 2. Feed u64::to_le_bytes(file_count) followed by each payload file sorted bytewise by its validated POSIX UTF-8 relative path (RelPath, / separators): len(path) || path || len(content) || blake3(content) (all lengths as u64 little-endian). - Represent ArtifactId as a 32-byte BLAKE3 digest formatted as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

Rationale: Because produced_by.run changes on every execution, hashing it made two identical deterministic runs produce different ArtifactIds, breaking NFR-2, FR-STO-4 (content deduplication), and downstream caching. Domain separation, length-prefixed framing, canonical JSON key ordering, and POSIX path normalization prevent hash-boundary collisions and guarantee identical digests across Linux, macOS, and Windows.

docs.title: D2 — Explicit mallops-core dependency allowlist, YAML parser, and schema isolation
docs.text:
Decision: - Amend NFR-7 to distinguish forbidden dependency categories (no ML/tensor/dataframe libraries, no cloud SDKs, no object_store, no database drivers, no HTTP/gRPC servers) from an explicit core allowlist: - Default core dependencies: tokio, serde, serde_json, blake3, tracing, thiserror, ulid, tempfile. - Feature-gated dependencies: - yaml (enabled by default): yaml_serde (0.10). - schema (disabled by default): schemars for generating JSON Schema documents for editor completion. - schema-validate (disabled by default): optional JSON Schema validation engine when requested, rather than compiled into default builds. - Remove schemars::Schema from BlockSpec's public API; use Option<serde_json::Value> instead. In v0.1, with: configuration is validated by Block::validate_config(&self, config: &serde_json::Value) (typically via serde::Deserialize). - Avoid adding async-trait to mallops-core (use Pin<Box<dyn Future + Send + '_>> or a dual native/dyn trait pattern).

Rationale — YAML parser selection: - serde_yaml is archived and unmaintained upstream and depends on archived unsafe-libyaml (RUSTSEC-2024-0449), failing cargo deny. - serde_yml is archived and affected by an unsoundness advisory (RUSTSEC-2025-0068). - serde-saphyr (MIT OR Apache-2.0, pure Rust with #![forbid(unsafe_code)], configurable resource budgets against alias bombs) is a strong future candidate, but requires MSRV Rust 1.89, which exceeds the workspace MSRV of Rust 1.85. Because the YAML parser is not exposed in mallops-core's public API, migrating to serde-saphyr after an MSRV bump will be non-breaking. - serde_norway is a single-maintainer fork, whereas yaml_serde is stewarded by The YAML Organization (yaml/yaml-serde). - yaml_serde (0.10) is actively maintained by The YAML Organization, dual-licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0 (permitted by deny.toml), supports MSRV 1.82 (compatible with 1.85), replaces unsafe-libyaml with libyaml-rs, has no active RustSec advisories, enforces recursion depth limits, and reports line/column locations on syntax errors. Parser tests must still explicitly cover YAML alias bombs and deeply nested inputs.

Keeping schemars out of public types protects mallops-core semver stability at 1.0 and keeps BlockSpec compatible with dynamic WASM/gRPC plugins.

docs.title: D3 — Immutable ArtifactStore, validated ArtifactId/RelPath, and auxiliary metadata API
docs.text:
Decision: - Introduce validated newtypes in mallops-core: - ArtifactId: 32-byte digest with strict FromStr (exactly 64 lowercase hex chars) and no unchecked string constructor. - RelPath: validated relative path (non-empty UTF-8, normalized / separators, rejecting .., leading /, Windows drive letters/backslashes, NUL bytes, and empty segments). - Harden ArtifactStore semantics: - put(&self, manifest: Manifest, payload: PayloadSource<'_>) -> Result<ArtifactId> accepts a structured PayloadSource (File, Dir, Bytes, or multi-file map), writes atomically (temp directory on the same filesystem + idempotent rename), rejects symlinks and special files, and verifies canonical paths stay inside the root. LocalStore::put marks stored files read-only (0444) and directories (0555) where supported by the OS. - get(&self, id: &ArtifactId) -> Result<Option<Artifact>> avoids exists + get TOCTOU races. - fetch(&self, id: &ArtifactId, dest: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf> has uniform semantics across all backends: it always materializes the payload into dest (read-only copy/materialization on LocalStore, download + integrity check on remote stores) and never returns a writable path inside the store itself. - verify(&self, id: &ArtifactId) -> Result<()> recomputes the canonical ArtifactId to detect corruption or tampering. - Add an auxiliary key-value metadata API on the store (or companion MetaStore contract implemented by every backend): put_meta, get_meta, list_meta, and delete_meta keyed by RelPath. Caching (cache/<key>.json), JsonSink (runs/<run-id>/lineage.json), and the v0.2 model registry (registry/<model>/<version>.json) all persist through this API.

Rationale: Making fetch a no-op on LocalStore allowed external blocks to mutate stored payloads in place, silently corrupting content addressing and cache integrity. Validated ArtifactId/RelPath types and symlink rejection close path-traversal and file-exfiltration vectors across LocalStore and external outputs.json. An explicit auxiliary metadata API ensures caching and JsonSink work identically across LocalStore, MemoryStore, and future remote stores without hardcoded filesystem paths.

docs.title: D4 — Core signatures (BlockSpec, Block, Context, Error, #[non_exhaustive], Transform, io_schema)
docs.text:
Decision: - BlockSpec: add version: Cow<'static, str>, use Cow<'static, str> for id and port/format/flavor strings, replace config_schema with Option<serde_json::Value>, return &BlockSpec from Block::spec(&self), and add optional hooks Block::validate_config(&self, config: &serde_json::Value) and Block::resolve_ports(&self, config: &serde_json::Value) for config-driven blocks (such as std/train.external). - BlockOutcome & cache_policy: Block::run returns Result<BlockOutcome> where BlockOutcome has Produced(OutputDrafts) and Skipped { reason: String, outputs: OutputDrafts }. Any downstream node with a required input from a skipped node is automatically skipped with Status::Skipped in lineage. Add Block::cache_policy(&self, ctx: &Context) -> Result<CachePolicy> (Deterministic { extra_hash: Option<Digest> } | Uncacheable) so source/external blocks invalidate when local files or scripts change. - Runtime-owned output commits: blocks produce output drafts (OutputDraft { manifest_draft, payload }); the runtime commits them to ArtifactStore, injects Manifest.parents from the node's actual input ArtifactIds, validates outputs against resolved ports, and emits LineageEvent::ArtifactProduced. Blocks never call store.put() directly for outputs. - Context: - Remove pub span: tracing::Span (the runtime wraps block.run(...).instrument(node_span).await). - Add cancel: CancelToken (cooperative cancellation built on tokio::sync::watch::Receiver<bool>). - Separate ${env:NAME} (interpolated into config and hashed into config_hash) from ${secret:NAME} (resolved on demand via ctx.secret("NAME") -> Result<Secret>, backed in v0.1 by a SecretProvider reading MALLOPS_SECRET_<NAME>). Secret is an opaque newtype with redacted Debug/Display ("***"), does not implement Serialize, and is excluded from config.json, cache keys, config_hash, logs, and lineage. - Provide ctx.config_as::<T>() for typed config deserialization. - mallops_core::Error: define a structured thiserror error enum (Config, Validation, Store, Runtime, Cancelled, Secret, InvalidArtifactId, InvalidPath, Block { id, source }). - #[non_exhaustive]: mark extensible public enums and structs (BlockSpec, BlockOutcome, Context, Artifact, Manifest, ArtifactKind, Stage, LineageEvent, Status, Error, CachePolicy, PayloadSource) as #[non_exhaustive] with dedicated constructors/builders. - ArtifactKind::Transform: add transform to ArtifactKind for fitted preprocessors consumed by package and serve. - Manifest.io_schema: rename Manifest.signature to Manifest.io_schema, reserving signature for cryptographic artifact signatures (FR-PKG-3, v0.3). - LineageEvent: add timestamp, block_version, seed: Option<u64>, Status::Skipped, and use Digest consistently instead of an undefined Hash type.

Rationale: These additions eliminate every known breaking gap between core issues (#1–#9) and downstream std/serving issues (#11–#17), prevent secret leakage and async tracing corruption, guarantee consistent parents and lineage events, and make the core API evolvable toward 1.0 under cargo-semver-checks.

docs.title: D5 — serve outside the batch DAG
docs.text:
Decision: - Remove serve from the batch DAG (blocks: in mallops.yaml). mallops run executes the finite batch DAG and produces a package artifact (gated by eval). - mallops serve [package-id] is a separate long-running command that consumes a package artifact. An optional top-level serve: section in mallops.yaml configures defaults (target package output, bind address, port) for mallops serve without participating in mallops run.

Rationale: A long-running HTTP server cannot be a normal batch DAG node: either it blocks mallops run indefinitely (preventing RunFinished and mallops run && mallops serve) or requires ad-hoc skipping rules. Separating batch production (run → package) from online inference (serve) gives both commands clear, composable semantics.

docs.title: D6 — Minimal Predictor contract in mallops-std for v0.1
docs.text:
Decision: - Partially supersede ADR-0004 for v0.1: keep Predictor (and LoadedPredictor) out of mallops-core and define a minimal contract in mallops-std shared by both evaluate and serve (implemented prior to evaluate). - Include flavors(&self) -> &[&str], executes_code(&self) -> bool, structured payloads (Json and Bytes), and batch inference (predict_batch). - Promote Predictor into mallops-core only before v1.0, once validated across multiple backends (linfa, external Python worker, ort/gRPC).

Rationale: Freezing Predictor in mallops-core before implementing a single backend or gRPC/binary inference risks an early breaking change (for example, locking into JSON-only payloads). Defining it first in mallops-std before evaluate fixes the dependency inversion between evaluate and serve while keeping mallops-core minimal.

docs.title: D7 — Explicit Trust model and corrected NFR-4
docs.text:
Decision: - Add a Trust model section to SPEC.md defining explicit trust boundaries: 1. mallops.yaml is trusted executable configuration: mallops run executes native blocks and external commands with host privileges, whereas mallops validate and mallops graph never execute user code or external processes. 2. Only WASM component plugins (post-v0.1) provide sandboxing. Native Rust blocks and external CLI/gRPC processes are trusted code (external CLI blocks run via argv without a shell, with an allowlisted environment and isolated workdir, but are not a security sandbox). 3. Model flavors that execute code on deserialization (pickle, joblib, sklearn-pickle, torchscript) are flagged (executes_code = true). mallops serve refuses to load them unless explicitly opted in via --trust-unsafe-flavors. Non-executing formats (onnx, safetensors, skops) and signed packages (v0.3) are recommended. 4. Secrets never enter Context.config, config.json, cache keys, logs, or lineage; ArtifactStore enforces validated paths, symlink rejection, and read-only storage. - Update NFR-4 in SPEC.md to reflect these exact guarantees instead of claiming sandboxing for all plugins.

Rationale: Documenting trust boundaries up front prevents false security assumptions (especially around pickle serving and external commands) and ensures v0.1 CLI and store implementations enforce safe defaults from day one.

docs.title: D8 — Explicit BlockRegistry in v0.1 (no inventory)
docs.text:
Decision: - Partially supersede ADR-0003 for v0.1: mallops-core provides an explicit, instance-local BlockRegistry populated via registry.register(...). - mallops-std exposes pub fn register_std(registry: &mut BlockRegistry) registering all feature-enabled standard blocks; mallops-cli and library callers invoke it explicitly. - Compile-time auto-registration (such as inventory behind an optional feature) is deferred until post-v0.1 if multi-crate ergonomics justify its trade-offs.

Rationale: inventory relies on linker ctor sections that can be silently stripped under LTO or unused-symbol elimination, behave inconsistently across static/cross-compilation/WASM targets, introduce global state that hurts test isolation, and add an unsafe-containing dependency to mallops-core. Explicit registration is deterministic, zero-magic, and trivial for v0.1's standard library.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• mallops-core contracts are internally consistent across artifacts, store, blocks, config, caching, lineage, and serving before issue #1 begins.
  • mallops-core remains free of ML, cloud, database, and HTTP/gRPC dependencies while gaining a realistic, auditable infrastructure allowlist.
  • ArtifactId digests are deterministic, cross-platform, and deduplicated across runs.
  • LocalStore and external blocks have enforceable immutability and path-traversal protections.
  • BlockRegistry is isolated and deterministic in unit and integration tests.
  • Accepted ADRs 0001–0006 remain untouched per MADR policy; this ADR records all supersessions and refinements.

docs.title: 0008 — Edge build profiles and on-device online learning
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted · 2026-11-22
  • Refines: 0001, 0007 (D5, D6)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The target scenario is "train on a server, deploy to edge devices, keep learning on the device". ADR-0007 D5 already separates the two sides: mallops run executes the batch DAG and produces a package, and mallops serve consumes it. ADR-0001 makes every standard block a feature of mallops-std.

Three things are still undefined: 1. ARCHITECTURE.md says mallops-edge depends on "std (subset)" but never names the subset. Without a defined profile, an edge build can pull in training dependencies (polars, external trainer) by accident. 2. Training on the device is mentioned only for federated learning (FR-EDG-4). On-device online learning, where the model adapts to local data and no aggregator is involved, is not covered. 3. It is not specified how a model that changes on the device stays consistent with D5 (serving is not a DAG node) and with the immutable store.

docs.title: D1 — Named feature profiles in mallops-std
docs.text:
mallops-std exposes profile features that only combine existing per-block features:

Profile Contents Excludes profile-server ingest, preprocess, train-*, evaluate, package, serve-http — profile-edge serve-http, pure-Rust predictors (predict-linfa, predict-tract), transform runtime, local metrics buffer every train-*, train-external, predict-external

Profiles are shortcuts. A user can always enable individual features instead. predict-tract adds the tract dependency, which needs approval when it is implemented.

docs.title: D2 — mallops-edge is inference-only by default
docs.text:
• Default features: profile-edge. A default build contains no training code, so there is nothing to disable at runtime.
  • online: on-device online learning (D3). It enables only the train-* features of backends that support incremental updates (D4).
  • fl: federated client (local training, sends only weight deltas to the aggregator, FR-EDG-4).

docs.title: D3 — On-device online learning is a finite DAG, never a mutation inside serving
docs.text:
On a device, online learning (and each federated round) runs as an ordinary finite DAG in the device LocalStore. mallops-edge starts it on a trigger (schedule, number of new labelled samples, aggregator round):

ingest(new labelled samples, e.g. std/ingest.mqtt, ADR-0009) → preprocess(reuse transform) → train(base = model of the current package) → evaluate(gate on local holdout) → package
  • base input port. A train block that supports incremental updates (partial_fit, warm start) declares an optional input port named base (kind model). The name is a convention of mallops-std, opt-in per block: a block that cannot update incrementally does not declare it, so wiring base into it fails at validation (blocks.<id>.in.base, undeclared input port). No core change is needed.
  • Every update produces a new immutable package with normal lineage (its parents include the previous package's model). The model being served is never changed in place.
  • Gate and hot-swap. The local serving loop switches to the new package only if the evaluate gate passes. Otherwise the run ends with the gate failure and the current package stays active.
  • Rollback goes back to the last package that passed the gate, or to the base package pulled from the registry.
  • Retention. The device keeps the active package, the previous accepted one and the base package; older accepted packages are garbage-collected (ties to FR-STO-5).
  • Reporting. By default the device reports only the metrics of each update (FR-EDG-3 buffer). Pushing accepted packages back to the registry is opt-in, because it sends a model derived from local data off the device.
  • Under fl, the aggregator round replaces the package step: the device sends the delta and, once aggregation completes, pulls the new global package.

docs.title: D4 — Portable flavors for edge
docs.text: Packages meant for edge should use non-code-executing, pure-Rust-servable flavors (onnx via tract, linfa-*). Online learning on the device additionally needs a flavor whose train block declares base (in practice linfa-* models with incremental fitting; onnx is inference-only). predict-external (Python worker) is not part of profile-edge. ADR-0007 D7 still applies: code-executing flavors are refused unless explicitly opted in.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• An edge binary is inference-only by construction. CI adds a check that cargo tree -p mallops-edge -e normal with default features contains no train-* dependency, plus an aarch64/armv7 cross-check of the default build.
  • D5 still holds: serving never becomes a DAG node, and on-device learning reuses the runtime, store, lineage, validation and gates unchanged.
  • Device storage is bounded by the retention rule of D3.
  • Incremental training becomes an optional capability of train blocks (base input). Not every backend supports it, and the validator reports misuse.
  • SPEC.md (§3.13, roadmap) and ARCHITECTURE.md (§2, §8) are updated together with this ADR.

docs.title: 0009 — MQTT blocks and MQTT serving transport
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted · 2026-11-22
  • Refines: 0006, 0007 (D5, D7), 0008

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Edge and IoT deployments usually move data over an MQTT broker. The reference scenario: on an edge device a sensor publishes readings to a topic, mallops reads them, the model predicts, and the predictions are published to another topic. The same data, once labelled, feeds on-device online learning (ADR-0008). FR-ING-3 already lists MQTT as an ingest source. mallops needs to: 1. read messages from MQTT topics into a pipeline (training data, online learning); 2. write pipeline results (datasets, predictions, metrics) to MQTT topics; 3. serve inference over MQTT: request topic in, prediction topic out.

MQTT is an unbounded stream, while the mallops run DAG is finite and batch, and serving is not a DAG node (ADR-0007 D5). So MQTT appears in two places: bounded blocks inside the DAG, and a serving transport outside it.

docs.title: D1 — std/ingest.mqtt: bounded read into a dataset
docs.text:
• Subscribes to one or more topic filters and stops at the first bound reached: max_messages, max_duration, or idle_timeout. At least one bound is required (validate_config), otherwise the run would never finish.
  • Produces a dataset artifact (format: jsonl by default, or parquet when the payload schema is declared) and records topic, timestamp and QoS per message.
  • cache_policy returns Uncacheable: the same config reads different messages each time. Once ingested, the data is content-addressed like any other dataset, so downstream nodes cache normally and the run is reproducible from the stored dataset.
  • Delivery. QoS 1 with a persistent session (clean_session: false, fixed client_id), so messages published while no run is active are kept by the broker. The block acknowledges messages only after its output draft is complete, just before returning. This gives at-least-once up to the block's return: a crash or a cancelled run before that point redelivers the messages on the next run. Blocks cannot observe the runtime commit (ADR-0007), so if the commit itself fails after the block returned, that batch is lost. This window is accepted and documented; closing it needs a post-commit hook in the core and is left to a later ADR if real deployments need it. Exactly-once is not offered: consumers dedupe by message id or payload.

docs.title: D2 — std/storage.mqtt: publish an artifact to a topic
docs.text:
• An ordinary optional data-output block with Stage::DataStorage (the same category as FR-STO-1, not the artifact store; see ADR-0006). No new stage is introduced.
  • Publishes one message per row of a dataset/features artifact (or one per artifact for metrics) to a topic template (e.g. devices/{device_id}/predictions) with the configured QoS and retain; with QoS 1 it waits for every PUBACK before returning.
  • Publishing is an external side effect: cache_policy returns Uncacheable, so a cache hit never silently skips publishing.
  • Output: a small metrics artifact (messages published, failures), so the node fits the DAG and the outcome is recorded in lineage.

docs.title: D3 — MQTT as a serving transport, not a block
docs.text:
• mallops serve and the mallops-edge serving loop get an mqtt transport next to http. It subscribes to a request topic, runs each message through the package's LoadedPredictor, and publishes the prediction to a response topic. This covers the sensor → predict → publish scenario without any DAG.
  • Configured in the top-level serve: section and never started by mallops run:
serve:
  package: package.bundle
  transport: mqtt              # default: http
  mqtt:
    url: mqtts://broker.local:8883
    client_id: edge-01
    request_topic: sensors/+/readings
    response_topic: predictions/{topic.1}   # or the MQTT v5 response_topic of the request
    qos: 1
    password: ${secret:MQTT_PASSWORD}
  • Delivery. Requests are read with QoS 1 and acknowledged only after the prediction has been published (and acknowledged by the broker at QoS 1), so every reading gets at least one prediction. Each response carries the request's MQTT v5 correlation_data when present, or its topic and message id, so consumers can dedupe.
  • A reading that fails validation or prediction produces an error message on {response_topic}/error (configurable) instead of being dropped silently.
  • Under mallops-edge, the same connection can optionally push the buffered metrics (FR-EDG-3) to a topic. gRPC stays the default for the fleet control plane and FL.

docs.title: D4 — Shared connection config, secrets and security
docs.text:
• A single mqtt connection schema is used by D1, D2 and D3: url (mqtt:// / mqtts://), client_id, keep_alive, tls (CA, client cert), username, password.
  • password and the client key accept only ${secret:NAME} and are resolved through ctx.secret() (or the same secret provider in serve). A literal value is rejected. Secrets never appear in config.json, cache keys or lineage.
  • mqtts:// is recommended. A plaintext mqtt:// connection to a non-loopback host emits a warning.
  • Incoming payloads are untrusted input: size limit (max_payload_bytes) and schema validation (the package io_schema in D3) before the data reaches the predictor or the dataset.

docs.title: D5 — Implementation and dependencies
docs.text:
• Lives in mallops-std behind features ingest-mqtt, storage-mqtt, serve-mqtt. serve-mqtt is part of profile-edge (ADR-0008), since sensor-driven inference is the main edge scenario.
  • Proposed client: rumqttc (pure Rust, tokio, MQTT 3.1.1 + 5, rustls). It must be approved as a new dependency and pass cargo deny when implemented. mallops-core gains no dependency; only ServeConfig grows the transport and mqtt fields.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• MQTT data enters and leaves the pipeline as ordinary artifacts, so lineage, hashing and caching downstream are unchanged.
  • Re-running a pipeline with ingest.mqtt is not reproducible from config alone; reproducibility comes from the stored dataset artifact, as for any live source.
  • Duplicates are possible on every MQTT path (at-least-once), and D1 has a documented loss window on commit failure; both are stated in the user docs.
  • Integration tests need a broker: an in-process broker (e.g. rumqttd as a dev-dependency) in CI.
  • SPEC.md (FR-ING-3, FR-STO-1, §3.10, §3.13, roadmap) and ARCHITECTURE.md (§7, §8) are updated together with this ADR.
  • A future streaming runtime (continuous DAG) could replace the bounded ingest of D1; this ADR deliberately does not introduce one.
